ranking.note: Lowered to P4: author states it is a draft reference implementation not intended for merge that vendors unmerged libsecp256k1 work, and its mempool-policy component is speculative pending a consensus decision — marginal claim on mempool review attention next to live policy bugs.

inconsistencies: #36328 (package acceptance returns TX_RECONSIDERABLE when trimmed) and #35286 (testsubmitpackage dry-run of 1p1c packages) touch the same package-acceptance result plumbing; review #36328 first, since the semantics it changes are what a dry-run RPC would have to report.

#36466 (make unstructured Taproot annexes standard) and #35882 (functional tests asserting the current 'bad-witness-nonstandard' rejection for annex spends) directly contradict each other: if #36466 is accepted, the new tests in #35882 must be rewritten. Decide the policy question in #36466 before merging the tests.

#29843 (relax standard script flags under -acceptnonstdtxn on test nets) and #36466 (relax annex standardness on mainnet) are both standardness relaxations but with very different blast radius; they should not be conflated — #29843 is test-net-scoped, #36466 changes mainnet relay policy and needs a policy decision.

#36214 (cluster limit enforcement during reorgs) and #35026 (lockpoint recalculation in removeForReorg) both exercise reorg handling in the mempool; #35026 is the behaviour fix and #36214 is coverage of a neighbouring path — no dependency, but a reviewer working on reorg eviction can usefully take them together.

#36367 and #35581 both sit on cluster-mempool/block-template machinery (chunk fee arithmetic vs. fee-diagram deltas feeding waitNext); #36367 fixes the arithmetic that #35581's diagram snapshots rely on and should be reviewed first.
result.notes: No PR in this list is category-critical: the strongest items are real bugs with bounded, recoverable consequences (reject-filter censorship under mempool pressure, fee underestimation, false reorg eviction) rather than fund-safety or exploitable DoS, so the list tops out at P2. Band changes were limited to one demotion (#36122); all other original bands were retained and only the ordering was tightened.
